overview: The Carson City Public Land Correction Act deals with federal land in and around Carson City, Nevada, and updates a 2009 public lands law that covered the area. It would transfer about 1,270 acres of federal land to the city at no cost for recreation, flood control and other public uses, plus half an acre for a road, with the land returning to federal ownership if it is not used for those purposes. It directs the Bureau of Land Management to sell about 356 acres to qualified buyers and to accept and later sell certain land the city offers back, with sale proceeds going to a special account for land-sale costs and buying environmentally sensitive land in the city. It also lets the city contract with outside operators to run places like a gun club, park and golf course on land it already received, and sets a one-year deadline to offer certain land for sale. As of July 23, 2026, the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee had approved it and it was waiting for a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say the bill fixes problems with an earlier land deal, gives the city land it needs for parks and flood control, and keeps sale money in the community.
against: Critics say it gives away and sells federal land, waives some of the usual planning steps, and does not require the federal government to clean up any contamination before the land changes hands.
